instruction: Let parse fields use strftime-style datetime formats (the 1989 C standard directives) as their type, e.g. parse('a {:%Y-%m-%d} b', 'a 1997-07-16 b'), '{dt:%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S}' or '{:%Y%m%d}'. A format spec that contains a supported directive is a datetime format; the existing '%' (percentage) type and every other type, including tg/ta/te/th/ti/tt/tc/ts, must behave as before. Supported directives: %a %A %w %d %b %B %m %y %Y %H %I %p %M %S %f %z %j %U %W. Expose them as a module-level dict parse.dt_format_to_regex that maps each supported directive to the regular expression it matches (tests iterate over its keys). The result type depends on the directives in the format: date directives (%a %A %w %d %b %B %m %y %Y %j %U %W) and time directives (%H %I %p %M %S %f %z) together give datetime.datetime, date directives alone datetime.date, time directives alone datetime.time. A format without %y or %Y uses the current year; missing time parts are 0 (parse('a {time:%M:%S} b', 'a 23:27 b') gives time(0, 23, 27); '{:%M:%S:%f}' on '23:27:123456' gives time(0, 23, 27, 123456)). %d and %m accept one or two digits ('{:%Y/%m/%d}' on '2023/1/1' gives date(2023, 1, 1)); %j accepts one to three digits ('{:%Y/%j}' on '2023/9' and on '2023/009' gives date(2023, 1, 9)); %f is six digits; %z accepts +HHMM and colon-separated offsets with optional seconds ('+0000', '+00:00', '+00:00:00'), giving an aware result; %b %B %a %A match English names ('{:%Y-%b-%d}' on '1997-Feb-16', '{:%Y-%B-%d}' on '1997-February-16'). These fields are ordinary fixed or named fields: parse('a {:%Y-%b-%d} {:d} b', 'a 1997-Feb-16 8 b') has two fixed results. For every supported directive except %z, a datetime formatted with strftime using all of them joined by '_' must parse back to the same datetime. Document the feature in the README and add tests.
